text:
Once, one time only, sweet and gentle woman,
        your polished arm rested in mine
(and against the dark depths of my soul
        that memory has not faded);

It was late; like a newly minted medal,
        the full Moon appeared,
and the solemnity of night, like a river,
        spread over sleeping Paris.

Cats beneath the carriage gates
        slipped furtively,
ears alert, or, like dear shadows,
        followed us slowly.

And suddenly, amid that intimacy
        opened in the pale light,
from you, rich and resonant instrument in which
        the brightest joy vibrates,

From you, clear and merry as a fanfare
        in the sparkling morning,
a plaintive note, a strange note,
        escaped uncertainly,

Like a sullen child, horrible and sick,
        who would shame its family,
and whom, for years, to hide it from the world,
        they had locked inside a cellar.

Your discordant note, my poor angel, sang:
        “That nothing here below is firm,
and that always, however much it disguises itself,
        human selfishness betrays itself;

That being a beautiful woman is a hard trade
        and is rather the banal labor
of the mad, frozen dancer fixed
        in a mechanical smile;

That trusting hearts is very stupid;
        that everything—beauty and love—is a snare,
and in the end Oblivion tosses them in a basket
        and returns them to Eternity!”

I have often recalled that enchanted moon,
        that silence and that languor,
and that painful confidence, whispered
        by the heart in its confessional.

translation.title: Confession
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Baudelaire. The alternating indentation and the beloved’s dissonant confession are preserved.
